chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Zur'a, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who died intestate (without leaving a will) and for him were sons and daughters, young and old, and for him were servants and slaves, and contracted ones. How should the inheritors deal with the distribution of that inheritance? He (peace be upon him) said: 'If a reliable man stands to distribute all of that for them, so there is no problem'.

key_terms.عُقَدٌ: Contracted ones (assets held in trust or specific contracts)

ai.seo_question: How should the estate of an intestate deceased be distributed if there are minor children and various assets?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of appointing a single trustworthy executor (wasi) to manage and distribute the estate of an intestate deceased, particularly when heirs include both minors and adults. It highlights the Shia juristic preference for centralized management by a reliable individual to ensure equitable division of complex assets like servants and slaves, avoiding the complications of individual partition. This ruling underscores the importance of 'thiqa' (trustworthiness) in Islamic inheritance administration, ensuring the rights of vulnerable heirs are protected under a unified legal framework.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from zurara, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who died intestate (without leaving a will) and for him were sons and daughters, young and old, and for him were servants and slaves, and contracted ones. How should the inheritors deal with the distribution of that inheritance?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If a reliable man stands to distribute all of that for them, so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Zur’ah from Sama‘ah, who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who without a will dies leaving behind male and female children. He has servants, slaves and assets. How the heirs must deal with the legacy? He (the Imam) said, ‘If a trustworthy man stands up to distribute it among them, it is not harmful.’”
